title: %wrap - word-wrap to a width
purpose: Insert newlines at word boundaries so each line fits within a width.
input:
text = "the quick brown fox"
tiny = "short"
exact = "12345"
expectedOutput:
{out}
out = "the quick\nbrown fox"
short = "short"
exact = "12345"
zero = ~
notes: Two required arguments: the string and the line width. Wrapping happens at whitespace; lines are joined with newline characters.
A width of zero or less returns null; a string already within the width is returned unchanged.
